sourceInformation.source: The Incredible Wizard (Astrocade, 1982), licensed from Wizard of Wor
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), JavaScript, Canvas 2D, Web Audio; AI Hub client 1.4.0; no runtime downloads
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original code-native volumetric pixel art, plum stone, brass and spectral teal
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid and Blob rigs, original lantern-rifle and procedural poses, wings, bells and spell effects
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-written music, effects and gibberish voices. Music defaults to 10%. Human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and simultaneous couch co-op; AI Hub 1–2-player host-authoritative shared-world co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited headless tests allowed; fixed-step command campaigns, packaged Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, standard pad stub, phone multitouch, offline Web Audio and two-peer Hub harness. No FPS gate. Physical controllers, real iOS, TV viewing and human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Read original manual and contemporary December 1982 feature; visually cross-checked manual scan and inspected archived hardware video frames. Exact historical AI and synthesis unknown.

testingFeedback: 13 distinct implementation issues were fixed during verification and visual review. Test-harness mistakes were excluded from that count.
2 critical issues: corrupted packaged JavaScript and blocked familiar routes that could stall progression.
The ordinary-command six-room campaigns and packaged two-peer shared-combat test. They cover bells, portals, every Wizard manifestation, score carry, victory and terminal shutdown.
The initial title-only Node smoke check was least helpful: it missed the packaged HTML parse failure. The packaged browser check caught it.
engineFeedback: The native Humanoid/Blob rigs, textured TileMap and sorted pixel renderer provide a consistent art foundation.

Initially assumed TileMap.center returned an object; it returns an array. Verified signatures, explicitly bounded retained GridMover turns, and replaced alternating Arcade turns with simultaneous game-owned seats.
The serializable deterministic campaign simulation, swept first-impact combat and host-authoritative shared-world adapter.
Keeping cell movement, world-space collision, visibility and native TV-shell input ownership consistent across devices.

No engine source edits. Registered original shapes and lantern-rifle, and added game adapters for invisible touch controls, portrait framing and live online overlays. The Hub client remains byte-identical.
A native serializable swept-projectile system and simultaneous-seat Arcade mode would reduce adapter work.
promptFeedback: The one-shot commitment, radar and bell tradeoff gave the game a clear source-specific identity.
The plan suggested artifact naming while TASK.md supplies the authoritative suffix; TASK.md governs. Human first-run timing cannot be confirmed in a headless run.
Integrating six authored chambers, complete input and saves, deterministic verification and shared-world lifecycle into one portable HTML.
Separate hard acceptance rules from tuning targets, and distinguish automated pilot duration from human first-run pacing.

aiHub.name: The Incurable Wizard
aiHub.tagline: One bolt. Six floors. No known cure.
aiHub.description: Enter a pompous sorcerer’s sealed menagerie with a lantern-rifle that sustains one bolt. Read the radar, ring the bells and cover a partner through six original chambers and a three-part finale.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD move; right stick / arrows / mouse aim; R2 / Cross / Space / click fire; Options / Escape pause; touch twin thumbs.
